newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner in 2 bln NOK offshore deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner in 2 bln NOK offshore deal.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Kvaerner ASA said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent with Esso Norge for the construction of a production ship for the Jotun offshore field on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Kvaerner said in a statement to Oslo Bourse the deal was worth about two billion crowns.

"To be worth approximately NOK 2 billion, the final contract will be awarded in late March at the earliest. It is conditional on approval of the development plan by the Norwegian authorities," Kvaerner said.

Engineering will be done by Kvaerner Engineering near Oslo. The hull is to be constructed at Kvaerner Masa-Yards in Turku, Finland. Kvaerner Rosenberg's Stavanger yard will fabricate the topsides as well as assembling and testing the Floating Production, Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel.
Kvaerner said Bluewater would contribute operational experience, the turret and the mooring system. The two companies will jointly install the ship in the North Sea.
"This represents the final breakthrough for our commitment to building complete production ships," Kvaerner executive vice president Tore Bergersen said in a statement.

The production ship will be able to produce some 90,000 barrels of oil per day. Other facilities include a living quarters and storage capacity for about 585,000 barrels. Measuring 232 metres long and 41.5 metres broad, the vessel will have a draft of 16 metres.
Jotun lies in 126 metres of water off the south-west Norwegian coast. It is being developed with a wellhead platform as well as the planned ship.
The announcement followed a Norwegian newspaper report last week which said Kvaerner was expected to win the Jotun contract.
